item.title: Oil prices drop more than $1 as hopes for Iran, Ukraine peace talks pressure markets
item.description: Oil prices dropped more than $1 on Thursday as hopes for progress in peace talks over the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine wars pressured the market. Brent
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: TOKYO: Oil prices dropped more than $1 on Thursday as hopes for progress in peace talks over the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine wars pressured the market.Brent futures lost $1.14, or 1.2%, to $91.62 a barrel by 0141 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures fell $1.04, or 1.2%, to $85.49. Brent rose about 1.4% and WTI 0.6% on Wednesday after hitting two-month lows the previous day. Markets are falling on expectations that behind-the-scenes efforts are underway to secure a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine and that it is unlikely the Iran war will escalate ahead of the US-China summit next week, said Hiroyuki Kikukawa, chief strategist of Nissan Securities Investment, a unit of Nissan Securities. However, given the uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, the markets are unlikely to suffer a significant collapse, Kikukawa said.Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed to a major prisoner exchange at two days of peace talks in Abu Dhabi that ended on Wednesday, although US mediators said differences remained on other major issues, including territory.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv hoped to achieve concrete results on resolving the war this year.Meanwhile, Iran will not allow even a single particle of enriched nuclear material to leave the country and there will be consequences if US launches new strikes, Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said in televised remarks.Washington has said nuclear issues must be part of any initial negotiations with Iran aimed at ending the eight-month-old war, while US officials downplayed the need for further military strikes.OPEC+ crude oil production jumped in October, led by a sharp increase in output from Saudi Arabia despite continued disruption to shipments through the Hormuz Strait.US crude stocks rose by 9 million barrels in the latest week, market sources said, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. Official data from the US Energy Information Administration is due on Thursday, delayed a day due to a US national holiday on Wednesday.

item.title: Global Market Today: Asian stocks mixed as Nvidia turmoil hits AI-linked shares
item.description: Nasdaq 100 futures fell over 1% and S&P 500 contracts lost 0.5% after Nvidia tumbled about 10% in late trading. The company’s board is meeting to discuss Huang’s future after he admitted to an affair with a woman US officials reportedly believe is a Chinese spy, according to a person familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: Asian stocks were mixed as investors largely shrugged off a leadership crisis at Nvidia Corp. that sent shares of the chipmaker at the heart of this year’s artificial-intelligence boom tumbling in after-hours trading.The MSCI Asia Pacific Index rose 0.2%, with gains in Japan, South Korea and Taiwan. The moves followed a strong US session in which the Nasdaq 100 jumped 2.3%, putting it on track for its best week since May.Optimism around AI had been fueled by CoreWeave Inc., which surged 25% on an upbeat outlook, while OpenAI’s quarterly revenue reached $10 billion and Anthropic PBC’s initial public offering was said to be multiple times oversubscribed.That enthusiasm was tested, with Nasdaq 100 futures dropping 0.8% and S&P 500 contracts losing 0.4% as Nvidia tumbled about 8% in late trading. The chipmaker’s board is meeting to discuss Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang’s future after he admitted to an affair with a woman US officials reportedly believe is a Chinese spy, according to a person familiar with the matter.The New York Times also reported Wednesday that Huang had a relationship with Nvidia healthcare vice president Kimberly Powell, citing multiple people who worked at the company.The turmoil poses a particular risk for Asian markets given the region’s central role in Nvidia’s supply chain, which includes Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. As the dominant supplier of chips powering AI, upheaval at Nvidia risks shaking confidence in the trade that has driven much of this year’s global equity rally.Read more: Stocks in news: Tata Power, Cupid, Garden Reach, ITC, Aurobindo Pharma and Vodafone Idea“Nvidia’s latest developments could weigh on sentiment across the broader AI trade, but we see selective opportunities emerging among semiconductor companies that can offer credible second source alternatives for critical AI chips,” said Gary Tan, portfolio manager at Allspring Global. “Near term, however, investor reception to Anthropic’s IPO is likely to be a more important driver of AI sentiment.”The fallout from Nvidia spread across AI-related stocks in late US trading, with server makers Super Micro Computer Inc. and Dell Technologies Inc. falling. Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Broadcom Inc. gained on speculation they could benefit from Nvidia’s troubles.

item.title: Bajaj Finance unveils share sale to raise up to $1.25 billion
item.description: Bajaj Finance has launched a share sale to raise up to ₹117 billion from institutional investors. This offering marks a significant event following a major IPO by Jio Platforms last month. The proceeds will be allocated toward repaying various financial obligations, including loans and debentures. A team of financial institutions is collaborating with Bajaj Finance on this transaction. Additionally, the Indian equity market remains active, having raised approximately $50.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: Bajaj Finance launched a share sale to raise as much as ₹117 billion ($1.25 billion) from institutional investors in Mumbai, according to terms seen by Bloomberg, in what would be the first major Indian equity offering since Jio Platforms's record $3.1 billion initial public offering last month.The offering, at an indicative price of ₹1,025 per share, represents a 4.99% discount to Wednesday's closing price. Proceeds from the offering will be used to repay deposits, loans, commercial paper and non-convertible debentures, as well as for interest payments, among other purposes, according to the terms.Bajaj Finance is working with Kotak Mahindra Capital, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase, IIFL Capital Services, Axis Capital and JM Financial on the transaction.The company's board on October 1 approved plans to raise as much as ₹175 billion from a 117 billion-rupee qualified institutional placement and 58 billion rupees from warrants. Bajaj Finance on November 10 raised about ₹58 billion by allotting 57.43 million warrants to its promoter and holding company, Bajaj Finserv, at ₹1,010 apiece.India has been one of the world's busiest markets for equity fundraising this year, with companies raising about $50.25 billion from equity offerings so far, compared with $58.78 billion for all of last year.
